Char'li gasped as he struck the hard floor of the den, gasping for breath as the air was driven from his lungs, the chieftain had forbade anyone from trying to reach the surface and Char'li had been caught. regaining his breath Char'li rose, wincing at the pain in his back and glanced around the room. the den had been stripped bare, the wood and bedding commandeered to fuel the tribes ever descending crusade. the den's entrance, once open to the tunnels beyond was now blocked by long metal bars preventing his escape. The walls of the den were as hard as the floor, it seemed unlikely that he would be able to escape without the use of some sort of tool but with the starkness of the cell the guards would surely notice any attempt and punish him severely.

---

At first the Med'ja had worked tirelessly, delving further and further into the depths of the earth uncovering new and unusual veins of ore, smelting them with their limited knowledge into crude and twisted tools to replace those lost in the earthquakes. Days turned to weeks and as supplies of wood and the chieftains sanity dwindled a strangeness began to settle over the burrows unseen by all but one.

Char'li had first encountered the strangeness while working alongside his brothers in the mines; at times when the hours had drawn long or a tool had broken his kin would continue to dig, clawing at the stone with nail and paw until flesh gave way to blood and pain shattered their trance. A result of stress and exhaustion Char'li had thought, unusual yes but certainly not unexpected in such troubling times. The trance like fugue was however not merely restricted to the miners as Char'li was soon to discover.

---

One evening while returning to rest Char'li came upon Sha'ne, traveling as she always did between the mines and forges, delivering food and water to the workers. Stopping to greet her he was surprised when she walked past without acknowledging him "Perhaps she did not recognise me" He thought, after all with supplies running low there were no more torches to light the tunnels and the supplies of lightstone were spread very thin with much going to light the miners helms. Char'li turned to pursue her and as light of his helm passed over her feet he discovered to his horror the trail of bloody footprints Sha'ne had left in her wake.

Grabbing her by the shoulders Char'li turned Sha'ne to face him, her eyes were glazed over, expression blank "Whats wrong?" Char'li exclaimed, Sha'ne stared blankly. Frightened and exasperated Char'li shook her back and forth, the vase in her hands dropping to the ground and shattering upon her feet.

The breaking of the vase broke Sha'ne from her fugue and for a moment she stared at her friend in confusion before doubling over in pain "Char'li?" she gasped "What's going on?" "I don't know" he replied, helping her lower to the ground before tearing his vest into strips "The last thing I remember I was filling a vase with water and all of a sudden I became very tired "When was the last time you stopped to rest? Or stopped for something to eat?" I'm not sure Sha'ne replied, grimacing as Char'li bound the strips around her feet.

With her feet now properly dressed Char'li carried Sha'ne back to her den before fetching them some water and food. "I think something very bad is happening in the burrows" Char'li spoke as they ate "People are becoming sick, they're hurting themselves, we need to do something about it before it's too late" "But what can we do?" Sha'ne replied "we don't even know whats causing it" "We have to warn the Chieftain, send word to the Shamans if we can. If anyone can find a cure they can" "But there are no Shamans" Sha'ne replied "not anymore, they haven't been seen since the tunnels collapsed" "That's why we need to see the Chief, we need to make him see reason, to find a way to the surface and send word" "But the Chieftain has forbade contact with the surface and much of what held our tunnels up has been destroyed or consumed" "we have to try Sha'ne, it's the only hope we have"

---

With the Chamber of Elders destroyed in the collapse Chief Ma'Ten had taken the old brewery as his new throne room and it was here Char'li found him, seated upon a throne carved from the very boulder on which he had sat when his mind first began to unravel. "Who dares enter uninvited" The chieftain barked, his voice dry and harsh "it is I, your highness,

Char'li, son of Dae'el" "Ahh yes" the Chieftain growled "He who defied the gods so many moons ago. What is it that you want oh defiant one?" "Please your highness" Char'li begged "Your people are falling ill, their minds are addled and they work beyond the breaking of their flesh, until their blood spills and their bones break. We must find a way to the surface and send word to the brotherhood"

"No!" The Chieftain replied "Never again shall those who walk the surface set food in my halls nor shall we seek them out" "But my Lord!" Char'li Plead "Our people are destroying themselves" "Listen well son of Dae'el" the Chieftain glowered, rising from his throne "Our tribe has not been so lucky as you to cross paths with the Gods and emerge unscathed, we have lost much and I would see our tribe end before I sought help from those who serve our wayward masters. There is no sickness here boy, nor spirit, nor curse of the Gods. There is only my word and my will. Now, leave me lest I succeed where Gods have failed and strike you down myself.

---

The Chieftain had rejected his protest just as Sha'ne had feared, there would be no aid in this venture. Char'li was determined, he would not let his tribe die without a fight and so with naught but the light of his helmet Char'li set forth into the labyrinthine ruins of the upper burrows.

Though it was true the Chieftain was mad he was not yet blind to the actions of others, he had anticipated Char'li's betrayal and had set a guard to intercept the young Med'ja, so it was Char'li found himself accosted en route to the tunnels and cast into the cell in which he now found himself. Trapped and alone within the Chieftains Madness.

highlight a group of mixed units. now remove only the tanks. assign that to group one and give it a defensive posture. Pull them behind the front line. Select all the tanks (which are mixed in with the other units) assign them to a group, give them an aggressive posture and issue a move attack order to reposition them.

Beginning to see the problem? Even ignoring the obvious problems with Android devices lacking the computing power of the modern desktop, traditional RTS has a very refined system for unit control which has become so prevalent that it's in virtually every modern RTS. Unit selection, grouping, and management can all be done very rapidly through modifier keys in concert with the mouse. You simply do not have the flexibility to do these things with a touch screen without inventing a slow, cumbersome interface to assist you.

Could you do RTS on android? Sure. There are tons of examples of people doing it. Can you do it well? No. Not really. The simplicity of the controls has an impact on what you're able to do, and how fast you're able to do it. This leads to simplified interfaces that in turn have an impact on the depth of the game.
